turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shame, you made it. I was stuck at the robot by the garage for twenty minutes, some bakkie just wouldn't move.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, we came the long way round. The radio had the cricket on, the Proteas, and I missed half an over with all the hooting.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): They were something like 180 for 4, Rabada was bowling. We nearly had a fight in the car about whether that catch was clean. Lovely day for it though, not too hot.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ha, I only saw the score at lunch. Right. What have you come about today?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): It's my left hand, doctor. I'm 68, three months since the mild stroke, and it's still a bit weak, and I can't stop thinking it's going to happen again.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. Show me what it actually does. Buttons, a cup, that sort of thing?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, buttons are a proper nightmare and the tea cup feels clumsy. It's not sore. The fingers just don't listen. Is that going to stay like this forever?

[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me have a feel. Squeeze my fingers, both hands. Ja, the left grip is a little down compared with the right, nothing dramatic. How's the walking, are you still getting out?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, round the block most mornings. It takes me a bit longer than it used to, but I do it. Is slower walking a bad sign, or, uh, am I being silly?
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He does go most mornings. I go along if I'm not at the shops. He's not been on the ground or anything.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): My speech was funny right at the beginning. That's what scares me. Does that mean another one is coming?
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): How is the speech today, as we sit here?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): It's fine now. The slurring went after the first week or so. People understand me, hey.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Any fever in the last while, hot or shivery?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): And a cough, or bringing anything up?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough at all.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about the stomach and the bowels, anything not right?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, tummy's normal and the bowels are regular.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight, has it gone up or down since the stroke?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, err, I don't actually know. Maybe a bit down, maybe the same. The scale at home is all over the place.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He still finishes his food. I wouldn't say he's wasting.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, we'll park the weight, that scale isn't helping us. Let me take the pressure... 152 over 88.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that bad? Too high? I take the amlodopine, the 5 milligram tablet, in the morning, for the blood pressure. Should you put it up?
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): 152 over 88 is a touch above where I want it after a stroke, but I'm not changing the amlodipine today. You've had the high blood pressure for years, ja?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, years now. And every morning I take asprin, a hundred and fifty mg, and at night the atorvastin, 40 milligrams, the cholesterol one they started after the stroke.

[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stay on all three, don't skip any. Aspirin 150 milligrams every morning, atorvastatin 40 at night, amlodipine 5 in the morning. If the hand is still the same in a couple of months, we might do a scan, but I'm not booking one today.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): A brain scan? What are you looking for? And if it gets worse next week, do I wait? Can I still drive to the chemist?

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the weakness suddenly worsens, or the speech goes again, or a side goes numb, you go to casualty, don't wait. Short drives are fine if that hand can hold the wheel, and from what I felt it can. I'll see you here in three months either way.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Three months feels long. What if I seize up from sitting? I get anxious just thinking about it.
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We live together, so I'm around. I keep telling him the morning walk is plenty.

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep that morning walk, don't add a big programme on top. What I'm seeing fits residual weakness from the mild stroke, not a new one today. Reception will book that three month visit as you leave.

spec.situation: Patient three months after a mild stroke with a spouse; slight weakness in the left hand; takes aspirin, atorvastatin and an amlodipine tablet; blood pressure read aloud; walking and speech discussed.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Patient says walking is slower; neurological category and severity mild are not stated.
bad.text: Slowed walking (category=neurological, status=present, severity=mild, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Left hand is not painful ('It's not sore').

Doctor specifically decided not to change amlodipine today despite BP 152/88 being slightly above target after stroke.
Doctor said the possible scan would be considered only if the hand is still the same in a couple of months, and that no scan is being booked today.
Patient asked whether the possible scan would be a brain scan and what the doctor would be looking for.
Doctor advised to go to casualty if one side goes numb; the recorded fact says 'a side goes numb' but not clearly that this is body-side numbness as a stroke warning.
